content.value_statement: Authentication flows can become inconsistent between client components and server routes. This skill provides focused Better Auth patterns for sign-in, sign-out, and session protection.
actual_capabilities: Shows email and social sign-in calls through authClient.
Shows how to sign out from a client component.
Shows how to read a Better Auth session on the server.
Shows a 401 response pattern for missing sessions.
Identifies the client and server authentication module locations.
Describes the AuthBar component role and session endpoint.
limitations: It does not configure Better Auth providers, databases, or secrets.
It does not define authorization roles, permissions, or access policies.
It assumes the referenced authentication modules already exist.
It does not replace security testing of an application deployment.

use_cases.title: Add client sign-in actions
use_cases.description: Use the email, social sign-in, and sign-out examples in a Next.js client component.

use_cases.title: Protect server endpoints
use_cases.description: Check the session before returning protected data from an API route or Server Action.

use_cases.title: Review authentication integration
use_cases.description: Confirm that client, server, and authentication status components use the documented Better Auth responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Add email sign-in
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show how to add an email sign-in action with authClient in my Next.js client component.

prompt_templates.title: Read a server session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show how to read the current Better Auth session in a Next.js route handler.

prompt_templates.title: Protect a Server Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a session check and a clear unauthorized response before my Server Action performs protected work.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my client and server authentication flow. Identify where sign-in, session checks, and AuthBar status belong.

output_examples.input: How do I check whether a user is signed in on the server?
output_examples.output: A concise session-check flow using the server auth API and request headers, followed by a 401 response when no session exists.

output_examples.input: How do I add Google sign-in to a client component?
output_examples.output: A client-side social sign-in call that selects Google and sends the user to the onboarding path after authentication.
Guidance to show the authenticated user avatar when a session exists and a login button otherwise.

best_practices: Perform session checks on the server before protected work begins.
Keep client sign-in actions separate from server authorization checks.
Return a clear unauthorized response when no valid session exists.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on client-side session state to protect server data.
Do not perform protected actions before checking the server session.
Do not expose authentication secrets in client-side components.

faq.question: Which authentication library does this skill use?
faq.answer: It documents Better Auth through the better-auth package.

faq.question: Can I use this skill for client-side sign-in?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes email, social sign-in, sign-out, and session-state guidance for client components.

faq.question: Can I protect API routes with this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a server session check and a 401 response for unauthenticated requests.

faq.question: Does it configure a database or OAuth provider?
faq.answer: No. It assumes Better Auth and its providers are already configured.

faq.question: Does it implement roles and permissions?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on authentication and session presence, not authorization policy design.

faq.question: Where is the authentication status component described?
faq.answer: The skill identifies the AuthBar component path and its avatar or login-button behavior.
